_note: The third survey of Smetlede's centre (31 Oct 2026): the houses round the church square and along Smetlededorp to the school, for tools/town/town.py. Plans from the GRB outlines and the laser scan's roof parts (data/neighbours.json, by index in `grb`); walls, openings, roofs and colours read off Street View (August 2026 where the car passed, else April 2023 or older) and the orthophoto. Positions in the model (x, z in metres), colours as seen (sRGB); no addresses, names, signs or lettering. A volume: four corners p0..p3, p0-p1 along the ridge (the low side of a shed roof); faces by edge (0: p0-p1, 1: p1-p2, 2: p2-p3, 3: p3-p0); rows of openings per storey from the ground up (w window, W wide window, n narrow, o small, a arched, d door, D double door, g/G garage door, s shop window, c carport bay, _ blank pier; a number after the letter is its width in m), spread evenly with `margin` at the ends, or `at` [s along the face, token@storey] with an optional third element: that opening's own settings over the face's ("y": [sill, head] above its storey's floor, frame, panes, surround, bars, glass ...). Some houses were corrected after the photos Yoshi took on 5 November 2026 (their `_ref` says what).

houses._ref: The long low house on the square's west side: painted brick in cream over a brownish-pink painted plinth, brown shutters, small-paned white windows, orange clay tiles with three chimneys; its gable end on the square in bare red brick; a lower brick wing behind.
The brick barn at the long house's end: red brick, orange clay tiles, a wide olive-green door on the street, a blank gable on the parking with wall anchors.

The corner house on the square's east side: painted white brick, a hipped roof of dark slates with three roof windows. Corrected after the photos Yoshi took on 5 November 2026: white, not grey; white frames; an open porch at the corner behind a white pillar, a display window over a panel of basket-weave brick, two narrow windows, a black glazed double door and two black doors; above, four wide windows of three or two parts, white guard bars across the side panes of two of them. No company's name or logo.
A narrow red-brown brick house next to the corner house: a door and window under two windows, white frames, anthracite tiles.
Painted white brick with blue surrounds round the windows and a yellow garage door, white frames, anthracite tiles; flat-roofed backs.

The renovated house across the street from the corner shop: smooth white render on a grey plinth, black frames, a black garage door, three roof windows side by side in anthracite tiles; its gable to the square with two small windows and two air-conditioning units. Corrected after the photos Yoshi took on 5 November 2026: every window black-framed with a row of small lights along its top, the black door with a glazed transom, the roof windows close together.
Grey-beige painted render, dark brown frames, door and garage door; a lower white annex with a brown garage door; anthracite tiles.
Red-brown brick, two storeys under orange clay tiles with a long slope to the back, white frames.

The small painted house next to the portal's gap: off-white paint, white frames, dark tiles. Corrected after the photos Yoshi took on 5 November 2026: two small upper windows, four iron fleurs-de-lis between the floors, three openings below in salmon-brown surrounds with arched heads (a window, the white door with its glazed head, a window), a black letterbox at the corner, its gable to the gap in stained grey cement render without windows.

A yellow brick house with a strip of brown brick at its west end; a long flat-roofed hall behind. Corrected after the photos Yoshi took on 5 November 2026: one house with its white door in the middle (not two), white frames in thick surrounds of brown stone, the upper windows in three parts with leaded diamond panes either side, a light grey stone plinth, the gable above the small white house hung with slates.

Grey-beige painted render with arched windows in white frames below, decorative wall anchors, a white sectional garage door, a blue-stone plinth, dark tiles and a brick chimney. Corrected after the photos Yoshi took on 5 November 2026: greyer render, four small square windows just under the eaves instead of arched ones, no roof windows on the front.

The new block of flats (newer than the laser scan, so heights from the photos): a red-brick ground floor with open carport bays and a glazed entrance, two storeys of white render with wide black-framed windows, a set-back top floor and a roof terrace behind a glass railing.

The chip shop by the school behind its forecourt: white horizontal boards on a grey plinth, a counter under a dark sign band with a green light along its edges (no lettering), closed by a grey roller shutter between aluminium posts, a framed poster case left blank, a cream annex under a lean-to roof; a low bench and a bistro table at the counter.

The café by the church tower (a Street View photo of April 2023 from the owner): a narrow two-storey house of red-orange brick whose front is a crow-stepped gable, four steps a side and a flat top; courses of cream brick at the gable's foot and round the sign board, two lozenges of light brick beside the upper window; that window in olive-green frames with a transom, net curtains, a light stone sill and lintel; below, a white panelled door with a sunburst fanlight in a light brick surround and a step, and a wide window behind a white roller shutter; a blue-stone plinth; a white sign board between the floors with a plain red panel and the café's name. Roof and sides as the laser scan and an older photo from Kerkhofstraat show them: grey tiles, a rendered gable at the back with a chimney.

The old barn between the café and the church: orange clay pantiles, weathered dark at the end by the church, a green garage door and door on Kerkhofstraat. Corrected after the photos Yoshi took on 5 November 2026: its gable by the café painted white over the brick, on a pale blue-grey plinth, with one window in a stone surround; its long wall to the square in grey cement render with patches (a filled-in opening, old paint, bare brick at its foot and in a band under the eaves), one small window of glass blocks, older dark brick towards the church.

On the lane past the square's north-east corner: a low red brick cottage with its eaves along the lane, dark tiles with moss and a roof window; in front of it a flat-roofed brick garage with a weathered rust-red door under a timber beam and a glass-block window. Corrected after the photos Yoshi took on 5 November 2026: old salmon-red brick, a window, a dark timber door and a window, dark brown frames with net curtains, heavy timber lintels.

On the lane opposite the café: a two-storey house of bright red brick with slabs of light stone over its windows and door, grey frames, a grey concrete plinth; at its north end an older bay of dark brown brick with a grey sectional garage door (a row of small windows, a door let into it), new brick patched in over it, a small window above, and a rusty letterbox pillar in front; dark slates; a long low back. Corrected after the photos Yoshi took on 5 November 2026: the timber barn door is gone.

Next to it towards Kerkhofstraat: a newer two-storey house of dark brown brick, a dark door with glass strips, white roller shutters (down on the photos of 5 November), a band of brick on edge at the first floor, a chimney on its gable to the street.

Kerkhofstraat past the fork: a red brick house with a steep gable to the street trimmed in white, a white door in a stone surround, a wide window with a flower box, three windows above and one in the gable; its side hung with dark slates.
At the fork towards the church: a detached two-storey house in light grey render on a dark plinth, white door, windows under white roller-shutter boxes, dark tiles; a low pale garage beside it.
Across Kerkhofstraat: a narrow two-storey house of yellow brick with a flat top, a window and a door below, one window above, a curved band of brick at the first floor.

West of the school on Smetlededorp: a three-storey block of red brick from the early twentieth century, segmental arches over the first floor's windows, a light stone band, two garage doors and two doors in stone surrounds, a square stair tower at its east end standing above the eaves, dark slates.

Further west: a two-storey red brick house under dark pantiles with a small gable over its middle, white frames under roller-shutter boxes, a door in a green frame, a wide brown timber barn door at its east end; a low white annex to the west; a flat-roofed workshop behind.

South side opposite: a detached house of brown-buff brick from the seventies, two storeys under a hipped roof of grey tiles with a roof window, white frames, a brown timber door, a white garage at its east end; flat-roofed rooms behind.
Behind the parking past the barn: a detached house of brown brick from the sixties under a hipped roof of dark tiles, a chimney, a balcony over the door, white frames; a wide flat-roofed wing behind.

Next to it: a pair of houses from the seventies in buff-brown brick, roofs of one slope rising to the back, wide windows below, a band of brown panels between the floors, brown frames and big chimneys; low rooms behind.

East of the square on Smetlededorp (older Street View): two houses of white glazed brick under dark tiles, a wide gable over the eastern one with a balcony of wrought iron, a glazed porch, white frames under roller-shutter boxes, a street lantern in front; lower rooms behind.
